title: Stitch validity: output match versus information retention
hypothesis: Perfect shared-task output agreement of a low-description stitched representation is insufficient to establish informational equivalence: private feature probes and interventions can reveal information absent from the source even when task logits agree exactly.
physical_object: Paired source/target representations with one common task feature and one private feature; linear output heads.
mirror_coordinate: One scalar shared-task stitch coordinate (select common feature); optional full affine upper control.
logical_multiplicity: Task output agreement versus recoverability of an additional target-private feature.

development.selection_metric: Only validate implementation and serialization; no hyperparameter selection.

paid_objects: source and target feature generators and heads

success_gate: A View can only be considered informationally valid if it preserves both shared-task outputs and target-private probe/intervention outcomes on every fresh seed, while beating structured-noise and unrelated-task controls.
failure_gate: If task output matches within 1e-6 on all fresh seeds but private-feature probe AUC or counterfactual intervention behavior is below native by >0.10, classify task agreement as insufficient; if unrelated/noise controls also match task output, reject output match as evidence of shared information.
boundaries: Synthetic analytic falsification only, not a learned-model or PA241 reproduction.
The private feature is constructed to be task-irrelevant; test identifies insufficiency of output agreement, not failure of useful shared task function.
